## Your own placement {#your-own-placement .smaller}

::: {.small}
- Rerun `try_spec()` with the choices that you submitted, in the workspace or in the browser lab: its last line places your estimate on the curve
- The placement counts the specifications of the curve whose estimate lies **further below zero** than yours. For the reference specification it is **`r placement_ref`** of `r nrow(curve)`
- The same count places the published result at `r further_below(mark_of("OA", "b"))` and 456AP at `r further_below(mark_of("456AP", "b"))`
:::

::: {.fragment}
Paste your placement in chat – hold – send on "go".
:::

::: notes
Your turn to be placed. Rerun try underscore spec with the choices that you submitted. The last line of its output is your placement: how many of the hundred and forty-four specifications lie further below zero than yours. For the reference specification it is seventy-one, almost exactly in the middle. The published result sits at a hundred and twenty, and 456AP beyond the end, at a hundred and forty-four. Two or three minutes, then paste your placement in chat, hold it, and send on go. [go] Look at the range in the chat. Every one of you can now say where your estimate stands among a hundred and forty-four justifiable alternatives, and that sentence, my estimate sits here among the specifications of the curve, built in this way, is a publishable way to report a robustness check.
:::
